bull_case_summary: TSMC has substantial current earnings and profitability. Round two argues that sustained economics can support a thesis without a board-approval surprise, while distinguishing current net margin from guaranteed through-cycle fab returns.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts that a surprise is not necessary but retains Taiwan concentration, capital intensity and overseas-capacity cash economics as the stronger objections. The premium snapshot valuation and extreme extension do not resolve them.
key_points_of_agreement: Board approval and dividends do not establish incremental growth surprise.
Ordinary-share dividend and US-dollar ADR EPS are distinct measures.
Current net margin is not a through-cycle return-on-fab-investment measure.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether existing profitability warrants meaningful prospective upside before overseas-capacity cash and concentration pricing are verified.
unresolved_uncertainties: Debt, FCF, capex and overseas-fab investment returns.
Matched valuation and entry conditions with extreme RSI.
